lead: Coalition bargaining dominates after the local elections: an ANC–MK Party deal could hand eThekwini to MK, while the ANC and ActionSA edge towards a Gauteng metros pact without the DA. October CPI lands today, a day before the SARB rate decision, with the rand near R17/$.

items.title: Proposed ANC–MK deal would give MK control of eThekwini
items.summary: Insiders say the ANC would back an MK-led eThekwini in exchange for MK support for ANC leadership in Msunduzi and iLembe. MK says details will be announced by Thursday or Friday; MK also wants a link to the provincial executive.

items.title: ANC and ActionSA near Gauteng metros deal, but Joburg mayoralty is the snag
items.summary: A draft would give ActionSA Johannesburg and Tshwane and the ANC Ekurhuleni, though together they still fall short of majorities in all three councils and need smaller parties. The DA won the most seats in each metro.

items.title: Report: DA floats Hill-Lewis for Joburg mayor in swap with Zille
items.summary: The DA has reportedly raised the idea of its leader moving to Johannesburg and Helen Zille returning to Cape Town to win over ActionSA, which rejects Zille as candidate. Hill-Lewis neither confirmed nor denied it; Zille played it down.

items.title: MEC seeks to appeal ruling that voided three eThekwini senior appointments
items.summary: KZN Cogta MEC Thulasizwe Buthelezi wants to take the Durban High Court judgment to the Supreme Court of Appeal. The court, in a DA-brought case, found the recruitment process materially irregular and set the appointments aside.

items.title: Police chief orders full resources for weekend mass shooting probes
items.summary: National Commissioner Fannie Masemola condemned shootings in Atteridgeville and Sweetwaters near Pietermaritzburg that left 17 dead. No arrests have been reported; police say they are following a promising lead in the Gauteng case.

items.title: Water outages spark protests in Johannesburg and Soweto as Tshwane restricts use
items.summary: Residents blocked roads in City Deep and Protea Glen over water and power failures. Tshwane is on Level 2 restrictions with fines from R5,000, and Johannesburg on Level 1; the problem is pumping and storage capacity, not dam levels.

items.title: SA summons Nigeria's new envoy over social media remarks
items.summary: Dirco's director-general held a démarche with High Commissioner Femi Fani-Kayode after he claimed his credentials-ceremony speech was cut and cited the President. The Presidency said he misrepresented Ramaphosa; the envoy called the meeting cordial.

items.title: eThekwini warns blocked and stolen manholes raise Durban flood risk
items.summary: Crews found manholes in South Beach stuffed with rubbish and bedding, with some covers missing, ahead of the rainy season. The city asks residents to report vandalism, which can also cause sewage spills and outages.

items.title: Iran and US trade strikes as drones target Bahrain and Kuwait
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched drones at a US radar in Bahrain, which the US says were intercepted; the US then hit a missile site on Qeshm island. Iran says three tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Trump begins Asia trip ahead of Thursday talks with Xi and Putin
items.summary: Trump arrived in Manila for a Quad leaders' meeting before heading to Shenzhen for APEC and a three-way meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, with Iran, Ukraine and nuclear arms on the agenda.

items.title: Ukraine holds peace talks with US and Europe as strikes intensify
items.summary: Kyiv held online talks with US envoys and European officials and agreed to meet in Berlin. Ukraine struck the Crimea Bridge in a record drone attack on Russia, while Russian strikes hit Kyiv.

items.title: Houthis advance in Yemen as government forces pull back to defend Aden
items.summary: Government-aligned forces withdrew from positions near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping lane, while the army reported hundreds of attacks on Houthi positions. Parliament voted to designate the Houthis a terrorist group.

items.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19
items.summary: An An-12 went down in an unpopulated area near Kemerovo. Preliminary findings point to equipment failure, and investigators are on site.

items.title: Five European states plan migrant return centre in Rwanda
items.summary: Germany, Austria, Greece, Denmark and the Netherlands are negotiating a hub for rejected asylum seekers, initially for about 100 people and possibly operating from 2027. Rights groups have condemned the plan.

items.title: Rand hovers near seven-month low ahead of CPI and SARB
items.summary: The rand traded around R16.94/$ on Tuesday and the Top-40 fell 1.2% as coalition uncertainty weighed. Economists expect October CPI, due today, to jump to about 5.2%; the SARB is expected to hold rates on Thursday.

items.title: Old Mutual selling 18 malls, including Umhlanga's Gateway, to Vukile for R16bn
items.summary: The R16.08 billion portfolio also includes Cavendish Square, Bedford Centre, Riverside Mall and Vincent Park. Separately, the JSE faces a possible penalty of about R340 million after a Competition Commission probe.

items.title: Hawks arrest two more in R635m Tembisa Hospital corruption case
items.summary: The suspects handed themselves over and are due in the Palm Ridge commercial crimes court. Officials allegedly split purchases below R500,000 to dodge tender rules.

items.title: Mofokeng double sends Bafana back to top of Afcon qualifying group
items.summary: Relebohile Mofokeng scored twice as South Africa beat Kenya 2-1 in Nairobi. Bafana lead Group D with 10 points, one ahead of Guinea, with two games left in March.

items.title: Bavuma hurt as Proteas slip to 386-7 before rain halts Wanderers Test
items.summary: The captain retired on 49 with calf discomfort, and three quick wickets followed. South Africa trail Bangladesh's 400 by 14 after lightning and rain ended day three; Bavuma is expected to bat again.

items.title: Ramaphosa leads 300-strong AI and investment delegation to Silicon Valley
items.summary: The 15-21 November visit includes meetings with Microsoft and investors. Ramaphosa says SA wants to help shape AI, not just use it, and noted the country hosts most of Africa's data centres.

items.title: US tightens AI chip rules to block remote access by Chinese firms
items.summary: A new rule targets Chinese companies using restricted US chips through overseas data centres. Separately, OpenAI is embedding outside safety evaluators from Apollo Research in a four-month pilot.

items.title: US senators want FAA router upgrade paused after nationwide ground stop
items.summary: Friday's four-hour stop cancelled more than 10,000 flights. Early findings point to network upgrades at two sites that destabilised systems carrying radar and communications data.
